definition: A design principle in which a model is trained to prioritize instructions from certain sources (such as a system prompt) above others (such as content encountered while browsing), to resist prompt injection.
details: Instruction hierarchies aim to give models a principled way to weigh conflicting instructions from different sources, an important building block for safely deploying agents that process untrusted external content.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. Think of it this way: A design principle in which a model is trained to prioritize instructions from certain sources (such as a system prompt) above others (such as content encountered while browsing), to resist prompt injection. And here is the clever part: Instruction hierarchies aim to give models a principled way to weigh conflicting instructions from different sources, an important building block for safely deploying agents that process untrusted external content. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. And that is Instruction Hierarchy — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.

citation.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
